The indicators summarise avoidable health and access inequalities associated with disability. They include mortality, noncommunicable diseases and physical or economic barriers; they do not describe inevitable consequences of a disability.

Education and childhood disability

The gap does not end with entering school. UNICEF found that children with disabilities were 42% less likely to achieve foundational reading and numeracy skills, as well as being more likely to be out of education at every stage analysed.

Compared with children without disabilities, children with disabilities were:
not to have ever attended school.

The percentages compare the educational situation of children with and without disabilities using relative differences. They describe a gap between groups, not the absolute proportion of all children with disabilities in each situation.
All percentages on this page are relative differences compared with children without disabilities. They do not mean that this percentage of all children with disabilities is out of school.
They are relative differences, not percentages of all children with disabilities who are out of school.
